_comment: What foundry_pull.py fetches, and how it is tagged. Folder roots are pulled whole (General/<bucket>/<Character>/<tier actors>); listed actors are pulled individually and grouped under the named character.

roots._why: work-in-progress characters; badged as drafts on the roster

actors.note: the 100 XP actor with the completed twenty questions; the other Shinjō Harunobu actor (FCqx2vUqaoQHEK5w) has none

campaigns._comment: campaign tag by character slug; anything not listed has no campaign

corrections._comment: field fixes applied on extract; the Foundry record has the typo

nasu-kogo._why: Foundry records 'Shoshuro Shadoweaver School'; the compendium roll spells it 'Shosuro Shadowweaver School'

tonbo-asahi.identity.school: Dragonfly Grace of the Spirits School
tonbo-asahi._why: Foundry records 'Dragonfly Grace of the Spirits'; the compendium roll has ' School'

iuchi-temur._why: actor records 'Iuchi Meishōdō Master'; the roll has ' School' on the end

portraits._comment: portrait path per slug, relative to the repo root

_derive_tiers_comment: characters Foundry holds at one point only; scripts/derive_tiers.py rebuilds their earlier XP tiers

school_aliases._comment: character school name -> the compendium's School Curriculum spelling. Use this where the COMPENDIUM is wrong: the source file keeps the printed spelling and the gate still resolves.

Isawa Tensai School._why: Fields of Victory p.79 prints 'Isawa Tensai School' (3 occurrences; 'Isawai' appears nowhere in the book). The l5r5e Foundry system's own core-journal-school-curriculum pack titles it 'Isawai Tensai School', and l5r5e-compendia-sortilege mirrors that. Upstream system bug; delete this alias once it is fixed.

promoted._comment: slugs promoted out of draft. The Draft folder and the Creator both mark characters as drafts; promotion is the deliberate act of saying one is finished, and is recorded here so a re-extract cannot silently undo it. Use scripts/promote.py.

title_aliases._comment: campaign-renamed titles -> the compendium title whose curriculum they use. The character keeps its own name; only the curriculum lookup is redirected.

Personal Advisor to Miya Misato._why: an Advisor title (Emerald Empire p.249) with a campaign-specific name. Corroborated by cost: the character's title records xp_cost 36, which is the Advisor title's cost.

ai_proxy._comment: deployed URL of worker/ — the Anthropic shim the published Creator calls. Empty until deployed; the Creator then asks for a pasted key instead.

concepts._comment: Loose concept material for a draft, written by the author. It is authoring context only: the Creator feeds it to every AI suggestion and never exports it, so it shapes a character without becoming part of one. Kept here rather than in src/characters/<slug>.json so a --force re-extract cannot lose it, and so it stays out of the promoted record.
concepts.isawa-chisato:
Isawa Chisato is a devout shugenja of the Phoenix Clan, serving the Elemental Master of Fire with the duty to defend the purity of the Tao. She believes that fire burns away falsehoods, and she has been tasked with destroying heretical teachings and ensuring spiritual doctrine remains pure. Though she seeks understanding, she is often impatient with those who do not see the truth as clearly as she does.

Her confidence is unshakable — she speaks passionately and forcefully, never softening her convictions. Yet, despite her outward certainty, she secretly suppresses her own doubt, fearing that her teachings could be flawed. She holds her parents on a pedestal, believing they set her on the right path, though she has never truly questioned their guidance.

Chisato finds peace in tending sacred flames, seeing fire as both a destroyer and an illuminator of truth. Her greatest accomplishment was purifying a tainted shrine, proving her faith in divine order. However, her harsh judgment of others and fear of being ignored sometimes alienate those who might otherwise listen, making her mission both righteous and isolating.
concepts.doji-sayaka:
Doji Sayaka is a refined diplomat serving the Doji daimyō, tasked with monitoring the Perfect Land Sect to ensure the Crane are not caught off guard. If necessary, she is expected to subtly undermine its leadership and cause its collapse. A master of diplomacy, she always speaks in extended metaphors, guiding conversations with elegance and intent.

She is impeccably dressed, maintaining an air of poise and control. She appears perfectly at ease with any outcome, rarely showing joy or displeasure, always maintaining a neutral mask. Despite this, she secretly struggles with sincerity, as her life has been one of perceptions and careful maneuvering, making true honesty difficult.

Sayaka occasionally disguises herself as a peasant, blending among the common folk to see the world from their eyes. Though she longs for genuine connection, she keeps others at a careful distance, fearing vulnerability. Deep down, she sees death as the final performance, believing that even in her last moments, she must meet her fate with grace and dignity.
concepts.iuchi-temur:
Iuchi Temur is a Unicorn shugenja and healer, sent to aid the Dragon Clan while ensuring that any affliction affecting them does not spread to his own people. His duty is to uncover the nature of the threat before it spreads, balancing his compassionate instincts with the need to protect the Unicorn. Though he follows Bushidō, he prioritizes kindness over rigid duty, believing that a healer's first obligation is to those in need.

Temur wears furs, his beard carefully braided, and his hair in a bun, presenting himself as rugged yet composed. He carries himself with calm reassurance, making others feel safe and cared for. Despite this, he suppresses his homesickness, longing to return to the one he loves, while fearing that his duty may cost him his own happiness.

He finds peace in caring for his steed and compounding medicines, yet he struggles to take care of his own needs, constantly prioritizing others before himself. Though he once contained a deadly outbreak, proving his worth as a healer, he fears the corruption of the Shadowlands most of all, knowing that even magic has its limits.
concepts.jinrai:
Jinrai is a former ashigaru turned monk, now a wandering teacher of the Perfect Land Sect. He believes that all people are equal in the eyes of enlightenment, rejecting the Celestial Order and spreading the sect's teachings to the common folk. Though he preaches peace, he struggles to let go of his resentment toward the samurai, finding it difficult to forgive their oppression.

His presence radiates determination and purpose, and he speaks passionately and inspiringly, ensuring that his words move those who listen. However, he suppresses hope, fearing that his efforts will ultimately change nothing. Though he enjoys luxuries when offered, he tries to live simply, though he sometimes indulges in a warm bed or fine meal.

Jinrai once converted a violent bandit to the Perfect Land Sect, proving the power of faith over force. He finds peace in chanting sutras, yet he secretly longs to be free of responsibility, growing weary of carrying the burden of leadership. His view of mortality is simple — his life is a sacrifice worth making if it furthers the cause of enlightenment.
concepts.kurosawa-genzo:
Kurosawa Genzō is a deserter-turned-rōnin duelist, wandering the land and offering his sword to whoever can meet his price. Though he carries himself with the discipline of a samurai, he no longer claims the title, instead forging his own sense of honor. He avoids pointless fights, only drawing his blade when there is purpose behind it.

His scarred, battle-hardened face still carries boyish charm, though he maintains a gruff default demeanor to keep others at a distance. He struggles to trust others, fearing betrayal or obligation, and regrets abandoning his duty, wondering if he can ever reclaim his lost honor. He sharpens his blade to find peace, a steady ritual that reminds him that he is still in control of his fate.

Genzō once spared a defeated opponent who later repaid the debt, reinforcing his belief that honor is found in action, not station. However, he knows that one wrong move could lead to an ignominious death, a fate he refuses to accept. Though he gambles on fights, he does not gamble with his own survival — he has lived this long, and he does not intend to die easily.

dsl_text_exceptions._comment: Catalog entries referenced by a character whose rules text cannot come from the DSL corpus. Each needs a stated reason; scripts/dsl_rules_text.py fails on any that is not listed here. A reason beginning DEFERRED is a gap Jordan has seen and chosen to leave for now — it is still counted and named on every run, never folded into the settled exclusions. Entries listed here keep Foundry's text and are marked text_source=foundry in the built data.
dsl_text_exceptions.Bō: The corpus states a weapon's rules as its stat line (category, skill, range, damage, deadliness, grips, qualities, rarity, price), which the sheet already renders in its own columns. Foundry's description is flavour prose with no rules content, so there is nothing here for the corpus to be missing.
dsl_text_exceptions.Calligraphy Set: DEFERRED (Jordan, 2026-08-30) — real mechanical text the corpus does not carry: a Core Rulebook personal effect. Converting it into titterpig-dsl-l5r5e is the fix, and Jordan has decided not to do that yet, so it keeps Foundry's text meanwhile. Deferred by decision, not overlooked.
